# Contributors

Thank you to everyone who helps improve **linux-rdaccess**, an experimental accessibility bridge between Windows screen readers and Linux applications.

Contributions may include code, bug reports, reproducible accessibility findings, documentation, testing with NVDA and Orca, braille testing, design feedback, and reviews. In particular, feedback from people who use screen readers and braille displays is essential to this project.

## Contributor statement

Contributors help advance the project's goal of making Linux applications more accessible to people using Windows screen readers. Each contribution is credited to the person who made it, with their permission. Being listed here recognizes involvement; it does not imply endorsement of every project decision, guarantee that a feature is accessible, or transfer ownership of anyone's individual contributions.

We respect contributors' preferred names, GitHub handles, and privacy. Please do not add another person's name, identity, or contact information without their consent. Contributors can request a correction or removal by opening an issue or contacting the repository maintainer.

AI coding assistants may be acknowledged as tools in relevant pull requests, but they are not listed as human contributors. People remain responsible for reviewing, testing, and submitting their work.

## Contributors

Contributor entries will be added here after the individuals agree to be credited.

## How to contribute

Open an issue or pull request describing your change or accessibility finding. For bug fixes, provide reproduction steps and relevant test results. Distinguish automated testing from live NVDA, Orca, and physical braille testing; do not claim validation that has not been performed.

See [AI development workflow](AI_WORKFLOW.md) for the repository's existing development and testing practices.
